item.title: Giant crocodile killed
item.description: A giant crocodile was shot dead this afternoon at Port Moresby’s Adventure Park after it attacked its handler. Initial reports and videos from the scene revealed the gruesome moment the crocodile mauled the staff member.
item.content:encoded:
A giant crocodile was shot dead this afternoon at Port Moresby’s Adventure Park after it attacked its handler.

Initial reports and videos from the scene revealed the gruesome moment the crocodile mauled the staff member.

Park officials and emergency responders struggled for several hours to free the handler from the animal’s grip. The decision was eventually made to kill the crocodile in order to release the victim safely.

St John Ambulance officers attended the scene and provided immediate medical assistance. The injured handler was transported to the 3 Mile General Hospital for urgent medical treatment.

His condition and the full extent of his injuries have not yet been confirmed by hospital authorities.

Adventure Park management is expected to release a full statement following investigations into the incident.

item.title: FRL to take Sepik development project discussions to districts and LLGs in West Sepik
item.description: Frieda River Limited (FRL) will take its community consultations on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to district centres and communities in West Sepik Province. The company will start the district town hall program in Telefomin on September 14, with meetings expected to follow in Vanimo Green, Aitape, Lumi, Nuku and Yangkok.
item.content:encoded:
Frieda River Limited (FRL) will take its community consultations on the proposed Sepik Development Project directly to district centres and communities in West Sepik Province.

The company will start the district town hall program in Telefomin on September 14, with meetings expected to follow in Vanimo Green, Aitape, Lumi, Nuku and Yangkok.

The engagements are expected to give communities an opportunity to question the company about the project, express concerns and hear updates directly from its representatives.

Local-level government representatives, community leaders, civil society organisations and members of the public are expected to participate.

FRL Country Manager, Dr. Joel Hamago says taking the discussions into the districts is important because not everyone has access to social media or other platforms where information about the project is being discussed.

He says the company wants to hear from people who may otherwise have limited opportunities to participate in discussions about the project's future.

Dr. Hamago says the meetings will allow communities to seek clarification on issues including project planning, environmental and social management, community development priorities and future consultation.

He says the company expects the face-to-face discussions to help communities better understand the proposed development while allowing FRL to hear directly from people who could be affected by the project.

The town hall engagements are scheduled to run from September through to early November.

The program will cover as many local-level government areas as possible as the company continues its engagement with communities across West Sepik.

The Sepik development project has generated public discussion in the province, making direct community engagement an important part of the ongoing consultation process.

item.title: Madang schools recognised by Education department
item.description: Six primary schools in Madang's Sumkar District were finally recognised by the Education Department this week after they were issued their respective registration codes by the department. The schools are Dylup, Imbab, Pepaur, and Budum on the mainland (Sumglibar LLG) and Kidoka and Taur on Karkar Island.
item.content:encoded:
Six primary schools in Madang's Sumkar District were finally recognised by the Education Department this week after they were issued their respective registration codes by the department.

The schools are Dylup, Imbab, Pepaur, and Budum on the mainland (Sumglibar LLG) and Kidoka and Taur on Karkar Island.

The schools have been operating for many years without any proper recognition by the department.

Kidoka is the oldest of the six. It has been operating for 20 years solely on community support.

Four of the schools are church- run, whilst two are government institutions.

Head teachers, school board members, and students from the six schools converged at Megiar Primary School to witness the occasion, which was described by the district school inspector, Wargem Wargem, a 'joyful moment' for them.

Mr Wargem said that with the registrations now sorted out, each school will now have six funded positions, beginning next year.

They will also start receiving TFF funds plus other benefits from the government.

Local MP, Alex Suguman, who was also present to witness the unveiling of the schools' code numbers, congratulated the schools on this milestone.

"I want to congratulate you on being officially registered as primary schools. As your responsible government, we will continue to support you. We are your partner and will work together with other partner agencies like the Catholic Church and the Lutheran Church to give you support.

"Sumkar DDA has given you some support through our Infrastructure Support Grant. Being registered is not the end of it. The next part is we have to work to elevate you up. We have to build more teachers' houses and classrooms.” Suguman said.

MP Suguman said his team will push to further develop the schools and put teachers on payrol.

He said that Sumkar before had a lot of educated elites who held high positions in both the government and private sector. That was about 10- 15 years ago. But now, we don't have it anymore, and we have to start doing something now to bring that back.

“Our vision since 2022 was to elevate the education sector in Sumkar District. So, now we are putting this into action, we the DDA will support you, and we will drive this together," Suguman said.

item.title: Madang police chief urges peaceful independence celebrations
item.description: The general public in Madang Province has been warned to celebrate the nation's 51st Independence Anniversary peacefully. Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim issued the stern warning this week, as police begin to step up operation, leading up to September 16.
item.content:encoded:
The general public in Madang Province has been warned to celebrate the nation's 51st Independence Anniversary peacefully.

Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim issued the stern warning this week, as police begin to step up operation, leading up to September 16.

He has also urged residents to respect the occasion and allow the people of Madang to celebrate peacefully.

In his address to the people of Madang, Superintendent Baim emphasized that this milestone marks not only a national achievement, but also a reminder of the sacrifices made by our forefathers and the responsibility of today’s generation to protect the peace they fought for.

“I want people of Madang to celebrate this first year of the next fifty years freely and without violence or any kind of disturbances. Some of us won’t be around to see the next 50 years celebration, so let’s all celebrate with oneness.

"Let us remember that Independence is a gift, and we must guard it with unity, discipline, and respect,” said PPC Baim.

He has also called on all walks of life, including churches, schools, youth groups, community leaders, women’s associations, and business houses, to come together in one spirit of unity and to ensure the Independence anniversary is marked by good conduct and lawful behavior.

“Let us celebrate as one people. We should not allow misinformation, hate, or bad intentions to create problems during this special time. Our celebration must reflect the unity of Madang and the strength of Papua New Guinea as an independent nation,” Baim added.

He reminded the public that independence was achieved without any bloodshed, and therefore, citizens must honour that legacy by maintaining peace throughout this period.

“We got independence without any bloodshed. Let us all respect our forefathers who had very little education, but with vision and wisdom, they fought for our future and achieved what they set out to do. Their efforts should inspire us to behave responsibly and uphold the law,” he said.

PPC Baim said the police will not ignore any unlawful action and any group that disrupts public safety during the time of celebration will be dealt with severely.

He also confirmed that police operations to flush out OBT rumours will continue during Independence and beyond in order to ensure that misinformation does not spread and that public order is maintained.

“Police operations to address ongoing OBT rumours will continue into Independence celebration. Anyone who defies the laws, spreads harmful rumours, or encourages people to act unlawfully will be seriously dealt with.

"Police will not tolerate anyone who disobeys simple instructions,” he said.

Baim also urged all business houses and private sector partners to support police operations by cooperating with security arrangements, adhering to event rules, and helping to ensure that businesses contribute positively to a safe Independence celebration.

“I call on business houses to support police operations. Your support will help us maintain peace, protect lives and property, and ensure that the celebration brings unity and pride to Madang,” Superintendent Baim said

item.title: Pangu Highway
item.description: The new road linking Port Moresby to Lae will be named as PANGU highway. Prime Minister James Marape revealed the name exclusively to this newsroom and said the name reflects the importance of unity among Papua New Guineans.
item.content:encoded:
The new road linking Port Moresby to Lae will be named as PANGU highway.

Prime Minister James Marape revealed the name exclusively to this newsroom and said the name reflects the importance of unity among Papua New Guineans.

As the country prepares to commemorate 51 years of independence, Marape says what better way to name a highway linking three provinces, the National Capital District, Gulf and Morobe, than PANGU Highway.

Prime Minister James Marape said the name PANGU goes beyond politics.

“Where Papua and New Guinea divide is, we put a plug, the plug will be called Pangu highway.

“Symbolizing it, as we step into 51st, in the midst of many issues, fragility in our own self, that Papua New Guinea must stand united.” PM Marape said.

Marape says Papua and New Guinea Union Party commonly known as PANGU was established on 13th June 1967.

It played a critical role in shaping the country’s path to independence and its ongoing governance.

“The name Pangu is a deliberate name, Papua and New Guinea Union, we must have a union, great leaders before us did not think rationalistic, but they came together.” PM Marape said.

The Prime Minister clarifies that the highway is not called PANGU because he is the current leader of the ruling party, rather it reflects unity despite differences.

“The road will be appropriately named Pangu Highway, not because Pangu government doing it. Yes, we're doing it, but it's just a symbolic of our two sides united.

item.title: Governor Rapa calls for immediate investigation on school protest
item.description: Western Highlands Governor, Wai Rapa has condemned the school protest staged on Thursday in Mt Hagen by a senior secondary school in the province. Governor Rapa said in a phone interview from Port Moresby said his government is prioritizing quality education as its paramount agenda for service delivery and for him to stay away from the province and hearing the incident is not acceptable.
item.content:encoded:
Western Highlands Governor, Wai Rapa has condemned the school protest staged on Thursday in Mt Hagen by a senior secondary school in the province.

Governor Rapa said in a phone interview from Port Moresby said his government is prioritizing quality education as its paramount agenda for service delivery and for him to stay away from the province and hearing the incident is not acceptable.

Rapa also said while the protest has turned nasty resulting in a death, he is deeply sorry and urged those in authority to carry out an immediate investigation into the death as well as the protest and enlighten the public and the province as to what really happened.

Governor Rapa said this is a first of its kind to happened in the province and for schools to take the law into their own hands is uncalled for.

The concerned Governor is sympathizing with the deceases family and tribe and said he too does not have any idea of what really happened and wanted an investigation team from the Provincial Education Board and police to get into this situation that has got way out of hand.

Governor Rapa said his government has and will continue to give priority to education in the province, and all stakeholders must also play their part in supporting and strengthening the education system in the province and not to jeopardize it in such way like protests, schools' fights or any other negative activities.

item.title: Preparation of MDA and immunisation under progress in West Sepik
item.description: Preparations for the Mass Drug Administration (MDA) and Intensified Routine Immunisation (IRI) campaign in West Sepik Province are progressing, with health authorities targeting a launch in the last week of September or the first week of October 2026. The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority says key preparations are now underway across the province, following a three-day Provincial Training of
item.content:encoded:
Preparations for the Mass Drug Administration (MDA) and Intensified Routine Immunisation (IRI) campaign in West Sepik Province are progressing, with health authorities targeting a launch in the last week of September or the first week of October 2026.

The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority says key preparations are now underway across the province, following a three-day Provincial Training of Trainers held from August 26 to 28.

A total of 91 participants, including facilitators, attended the training, with district teams now returning to their respective areas to prepare for health facility-level training.

The health authority says all MDA logistics have arrived in Vanimo, with sorting and packing completed and distribution to districts now underway.

The second lot of supplies was moved to Aitape and Lumi on September 2, while distribution to Nuku, Vanimo Green and other areas is continuing.

The logistics team is expected to complete distribution to the districts by September 7, while arrangements are being made to transport supplies to Telefomin through an MAF air charter.

However, the campaign continues to face a funding shortfall of about K1.6 million.

The Provincial Health Authority is seeking additional financial support from the National Department of Health, Sandaun Provincial Government and District Development Authorities.

The authority has allocated K500,000 from its Health Function Grant towards MDA and IRI preparedness and implementation.

Meanwhile, a planned Digicel SMS awareness campaign is expected to reach around 39,000 subscribers across West Sepik Province.

Health authorities have also developed MDA and IRI radio jingles in Tok Pisin and English, which will be broadcast through NBC Radio Sandaun in Vanimo, as well as Radio Maria and Radio Light in Nuku.

A fortnightly live talk-back program on Radio Sandaun is also being arranged to provide further information and public engagement on the campaign.

Social media, newsletters, banners, billboards and advocacy meetings will also be used to support public awareness.

The province is continuing its routine immunisation activities alongside preparations for the MDA campaign.

Aitape-Lumi has started its round three routine immunisation, while Nuku and Vanimo Green are preparing for their round three activities. Telefomin will conduct its round two immunisation activities.

At district level, Nuku Health Centre has already started health facility-level training, while other districts are preparing to begin their training.

Provincial emergency team have also confirmed the record of rainfall across all districts over the past two weeks, it has improved water supplies at health facilities and staff accommodation following prolonged dry conditions.

The rainfall has also improved access to waterways in some riverine areas.

However, health authorities are monitoring the possibility of flooding affecting the movement of MDA supplies if roads and rivers become affected.

Districts are expected to complete round three routine immunisation activities by September 16, while all health facility-level MDA and IRI training is expected to be completed by September 25.

The West Sepik Provincial Health Authority says preparations and awareness activities will continue as the province moves towards the planned MDA and IRI campaign launch.

item.title: Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School temporarily suspended
item.description: The Western Highlands Provincial Education Board (WH PEB) in an urgent notice dated 04th September 2026, has temporarily suspended Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School for a week. This suspension follows after the students from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School staged an "illegal" protest at the school ground yesterday morning calling for the step down of their school principal.
item.content:encoded:
The Western Highlands Provincial Education Board (WH PEB) in an urgent notice dated 04th September 2026, has temporarily suspended Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School for a week.

This suspension follows after the students from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School staged an "illegal" protest at the school ground yesterday morning calling for the step down of their school principal.

PEB Chairman and Education Executive Manager, Tony Buldung, in a press brief today in Mt Hagen said the suspension of the school also includes the suspension of the school principal and the school's board of governors.

" Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School will be suspended for one week while pending investigation into the school students protest yesterday (030926) that has led to the death of a Grade 11 student," Buldung said.

Mr. Buldung added the suspension is expected to last for only one schooling week and a decision will follow suit.

PEB Deputy Chairman, Leo Meninga stressed that the PEB has request all student leaders, teachers, school administration, and board of governors to give their full cooperation towards the investigation.

" All stakeholders of the school must fully cooperate with the investigation team into the protest which has caused a death so that the culprits involved can be identified and dealt with accordingly," Meninga said.

He added that while the school is under suspension, the PEB has strictly refrain students, teachers and board members from accessing the school's premises until the school is officially opened.

The PEB headed by Chairman Tony Buldung has also extended their apology to what had happened and the relatives and immediate family members of the deceased student.

Moreover, PEB Chairman has also cleared the air that the office of the PEB and respective education offices has not received any petition or complaint from the students prior to their strike and was shocked to receive the news of the students’ protest.

Meantime, a Grade 11 student from Kui Wamp Nga Secondary School has been confirmed dead in regards to the protest and many students and by standers were injured including several police officers who were seriously injured and treated at the Mt Hagen Provincial Specialist Hospital.

The students of Kui Wamp Nga Secondary staged a protest yesterday at their school and attempted to deliver their petition to the education office at Mara Haus- the provincial headquarter.

They were however stopped along the highway and the story still remains unclear who instigated or what transpired there that had ignited the protest to turn nasty leaving one dead and many injured.
